html:
The Tongva are an Indigenous people of California from the Los Angeles Basin and the southern Channel Islands, an area of about 4,000 square miles. Before colonisation they lived in as many as 100 villages and named themselves by village, not by one tribal name. They speak a Takic language of the Uto-Aztecan family.

They fished from plank canoes, gathered acorns and seeds, and traded soapstone from Santa Catalina Island along the coast. Their neighbours were the Chumash to the west, the Serrano in the mountains and the Acjachemen to the south.

The Spanish called them Gabrieleño and Fernandeño, after Mission San Gabriel, founded in 1771, and Mission San Fernando. In 1785 a Tongva healer, Toypurina, helped lead a revolt against San Gabriel. Disease and forced labour cut their numbers. Some families also use the name Kizh.
